title: 2007 AMC 12B Problem 19
statement: Rhombus \(ABCD,\) with side length \(6,\) is rolled to form a cylinder of volume \(6\) by taping \(\overline{AB}\) to \(\overline{DC}.\) What is \(\sin(\angle ABC)?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(\theta=\angle ABC.\) The base circle has circumference \(6,\) so its radius is \(\dfrac{6}{2\pi}=\dfrac3\pi.\) The height of the cylinder is the rhombus altitude \(6\sin\theta.\)

The volume is \[ \pi\left(\dfrac3\pi\right)^2(6\sin\theta)=\dfrac{54}{\pi}\sin\theta=6, \] so \(\sin\theta=\dfrac{\pi}{9}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: Taping \(\overline{AB}\) to \(\overline{DC}\) makes a side of length \(6\) the base circumference, so the radius is \(\frac{3}{\pi}\)
The cylinder’s height is the rhombus altitude \(6\sin\theta;\) set the volume equal to \(6\)
